V1.name: one retention authority

design.policy: `HistoryRange { Full, Trailing(usize) }` in exec/kv.rs beside LayerKvGeometry, with `HistoryRange::of_span(span, window)` — ONE exhaustive match over AttentionSpan, the only place the policy is written — and `required_range(position) -> Range<usize>` (= required_start(position)..position + 1).
design.mapping: Sliding + Some(w) → Trailing(w); Sliding + None → Full (no declared bound to apply); Full → Full; Windowed → Full (its extent is spatial, not a position count — the AttentionSpan::Windowed doc already forbids inferring dead positions from it). Exactly the two formulas it replaces.
design.plan_owned: `AttentionOp::history()` = of_span(op.span, op.window). LayerKvGeometry gains `history: HistoryRange`, set from the plan op in plan_continuation_geometry (ConvQkv and any other KV side: Full), so the authority reaches providers (B needs it in V4). `window` stays a geometry fact, informational as before.
design.backends: reference, production and device take their floor from `call.history().required_range(position).start`, where `AttentionCall::history()` = of_span(call.span, call.window) — the call's span and window are copied from the plan op at the one construction site (exec/mod.rs). production's `source_start` becomes a thin call to it (device reuses it); reference's local match is deleted.
design.why_a_field_on_geometry: `LayerKvGeometry.window` is copied from op.window regardless of span (exec/continuation.rs:260). A provider that read `window` alone would drop rows on a Full or Windowed layer carrying Some(w). The span-aware authority must travel with the geometry.
design.not_changed: larql-compute's `window_start` (V2 GQA) and the Metal lowering's window: different paths, outside VIEW-1's backends

what_landed: exec/kv.rs: `HistoryRange { Full, Trailing(usize) }`, `of_span` (the one exhaustive policy match), `required_start` / `required_range`; `AttentionOp::history()`; `LayerKvGeometry.history` plus `LayerKvGeometry::required_range`; `window` re-documented as a geometry fact, not a retention permission
exec/continuation.rs: plan_continuation_geometry sets `history` from the op (softmax) and `Full` (conv-QKV)
exec/production.rs: `source_start` reads the authority (device reuses it); exec/reference.rs: its local match deleted. Neither backend imports AttentionSpan any more.

representation.choice: a trait object behind a Copy struct: `KvView<'a> { base, end, keys: &'a (dyn KvRows + Sync), values: &'a (dyn KvRows + Sync) }` over the one-method trait `KvRows { fn row(&self, position: usize) -> &[f32] }`, where `position` is ABSOLUTE. New module exec/kv_view.rs.
representation.why_not_an_enum: a closed enum (Rows | Contiguous | …) would make every future backing — paged, codec-backed, an external plugin's own layout — a change to core's enum. The freeze asks for a general view, not one shaped by today's two providers. The trait object keeps it open.
representation.why_not_generic: a generic parameter on AttentionStepCall would propagate through PlanBackend (object-safe today, held as &dyn and Arc<dyn>); a trait object keeps the backend trait object-safe.
representation.cost_and_its_measurement: one virtual call per row fetch, in the same place the kernels already call `key_of(p)`/`value_of(p)` closures per position. Measured, not assumed: decode ms/token on qwen3-0.6b (ProductionBackend, 512-token prefill, 64 decode steps), main vs V2, alternating, 3 repeats each; recorded here before V2 merges.
representation.Sync: the kernels' closures may be called from worker threads, so the rows are `dyn KvRows + Sync`

refusal.type: `ViewRefusal { needed: Range<usize>, base, end }` — names the positions the plan requires and what the view holds; converts to VindexError
refusal.unbypassable: AttentionStepCall's view becomes PRIVATE; the only constructor, `AttentionStepCall::new(op, position, rows)`, checks `op.history().required_range(position)` (its history part, start..position) against [base, end) and that end == position. A step whose view drops a required row cannot be built, so no backend ever receives one (S3 on every backend by construction). The view's own key(p)/value(p) assert base <= p < end with a named message; after the constructor's check that is unreachable, and it is an executor bug, not a retention one, if ever hit.
refusal.conv_qkv: its history requirement is Full; the executor checks covers(0..base) before the operator, the same refusal

migration.index_sites: the 6 `step.keys[p]` / `step.values[p]` (reference, production, device) become `rows.key(p)` / `rows.value(p)`; `p == position` still returns the fresh row
migration.conv_qkv: `layer_forward_with(past: KvView, base, …)`; `key_at` / `value_at` / `visible` read past.end() instead of past_keys.len()
migration.providers_unchanged: the trait keeps keys()/values() in V2; the executor wraps them with `KvView::over_rows` (base 0). The provider trait and ABI change in V3.
migration.conv_qkv_copy_kept: the executor still copies ConvQkv's rows before taking &mut recurrent_state (behaviour-neutral); Q1 re-measures after V2 and again after V3
migration.construction_sites: 2 production (exec/mod.rs attention_into_kv, exec/decode.rs) and 4 test sites move to AttentionStepCall::new

V3.name: providers
scope: provider migration (row/v1, canonical/v1 loses its mirror, C5 HostileRows + the C6 fixture, the test doubles, MEM-1's Measured)

trait.change: `keys(&self, layer) -> &[Vec<f32>]` and `values(&self, layer) -> &[Vec<f32>]` are replaced by ONE method `rows(&self, layer) -> KvView<'_>`. ContinuationProvider goes from 9 methods to 8.
trait.why_one_method: K and V are always lent together over one [base, end); two methods let a provider lend mismatched lengths, which KvView::over_rows today has to assert against. One method makes the mismatch unrepresentable.

canonical.change: canonical/v1 lends its authoritative matrices directly; the `rows: Vec<LayerRows>` mirror, `LayerRows` and `from_matrices` are DELETED (append no longer copies each row twice; from_cache no longer rebuilds the mirror).
canonical.backing: KvView gains a third backing, `Contiguous { data: &[f32], width }` for K and V, read by static dispatch: row p at data[(p - base)·width ..]. Constructor `KvView::contiguous(base, width, keys, values)` refuses slices that are not whole rows or differ in length.
canonical.why_not_Dyn: the orphan rule forbids larql-kv implementing larql-vindex's KvRows for ndarray's Array2; a newtype would work, but contiguous row-major storage is a fundamental layout (paged and windowed contiguous stores will use it too) and deserves the static path the Rows backing has. Dyn stays for everything else.
canonical.layout: KvCache's Array2 is grown by push_row on axis 0 and is row-major; `as_slice()` must be Some. If it ever is not (a view or transposed matrix), canonical refuses by name rather than copying — a silent copy is exactly the mirror V3 removes.

V3.row_v1: rows(layer) = KvView::over_rows(&keys, &values): no allocation, no copy (the V2 fast path)

B.provider: `ExactRetention` in crates/larql-kv/tests/continuation_mem_1 (the MEM-1 harness, so its allocator instruments apply). Rows held one allocation per position (it adopts the backend's rows, as row/v1 does), per layer with its own base; prepare() records each layer's HistoryRange from the plan geometry — the provider never reads `window` itself. After appending position p on a layer it drops every row below `history.required_start(p)` and lends `KvView::rows_from(base, …)`.
B.frozen_formula_reading: the freeze's 'base == required_range(position).start and end == position + 1 after every append' is followed exactly with position = the position just appended: a sliding layer keeps w rows [p+1−w, p]. The next step (at p+1) reads [p+2−w, p+1] of which p+1 is fresh, so one held row is one more than strictly needed — a superset, which the retention rule permits. Recorded so nobody later reads it as the tightest possible retention.
four_conditions_together: after every append, per layer: base == HistoryRange.required_start(p) (sliding: p+1−w; full: 0), checked by the provider on itself and recorded
end == p + 1 (end is logical: every row ever appended)

every dropped row is PHYSICALLY freed: its own K and V allocations (by pointer, as adopted) are freed inside the append scope that drops them — the backend made them outside any measured scope, so they were never in the live table and 'absent from the table' would prove nothing; a free event for that exact address does
logits bit-identical to row/v1 on the sliding fixture and on gemma3-4b-it past its window (1,100-position prefill, window 1,024), every phase
B.resident: at the end, rows held per sliding layer = w (1,024 on gemma), per full layer = n
